breath.songTitle: I Saw Her for the First Time
breath.line: When she walked in I held my breath
stanza: When she walked in I held my breath
I thought I might just die
When she came way and she caught my eye
I felt like I could cry

breath.line: I could taste the fire on your breath
stanza: I wanted that heat so bad
I could taste the fire on your breath
And I wanted in your storm so bad
I could taste the lightning on your breath
I used to call you on the telephone
I couldn't catch my breath
To expel a single word
You would hang up your telephone
You always looked confused
Then you'd turn and close the blinds

breath.line: Officer, please, don't check my breath
stanza: Keep both eyes on the road tonight
'Cause God knows where I've been
Officer, please, don't check my breath
That ain't my only sin

breath.line: It was me tearing out the baby's breath
stanza: And each day I looked out on the lawn
And I wondered what all was gone
Until I saw it was lucky old me
How could I run without losing anything?
How could I run without becoming lean?
It was agreed
It was a greed
It was me tearing out the baby's breath
There's bourbon on the breath
Of the singer you love so much
He takes all his words from the books
That you don't read anyway

breath.line: That it's precious as a baby's breath
stanza: I hear them say that this life is a gift
That it's precious as a baby's breath
They can talk to a door
When my time has come
Open up the doors of heaven and let me in

breath.line: Down to the very last breath
stanza: The children on Melrose strut their stuff
Is absolute zero cold enough?
And out in the valley, warm and clean
The little ones sit by the TV screen
No thoughts to think
No tears to cry
All sucked dry
Down to the very last breath
Do you want to love me more?
Do you want to love me more?
For love is the breath
If water and wave
Is cursed by the same thing
That nurtured its shame
Is it worth all the work?

breath.line: Spread your arms and hold your breath
stanza: Well, he's one of those who knows
That life is just a leap of faith
Spread your arms and hold your breath
And always trust your cape
You laugh until you cry
You cry until you laugh
And everyone must breathe
Until their dying breath

breath.line: Eventually the dying man takes his final breath
stanza: Eventually the dying man takes his final breath
But first checks his news feed to see what he's 'bout to miss
And it occurs to him a little late in the game
We leave as clueless as we came
From the rented heavens to the shadows in the cave
We'll all be wrong someday

breath.line: 'Cause I felt I had to justify each breath
stanza: So I went running down a list of things
Some were real, but on some of them, I lied
'Cause I felt I had to justify each breath
That I'd been breathing in this life
Then I realized I was playing into someone else's rules
Trying to keep my score up in a game I did not choose
Then I looked that ghost straight in the eye
And said "You had better not be coming back by again"

breath.line: I can smell the sorrow on your breath
stanza: Look up, and what do you see?
All of you and all of me, fluorescent and starry
And some of them, they surprise
I can't look it in the eyes, Seconal, Spanish fly, absinthe, kerosene
Cherry-flavored neck and collar
I can smell the sorrow on your breath
The sweat, the victory and sorrow, the smell of fear
I got it

breath.line: One's got the diesel fuel on her breath
stanza: One's got the diesel fuel on her breath
One's got the damp taste of the earth on it
Two blue lights
Words under my breath
Float through the ceiling

breath.line: She pauses in her every breath
stanza: Lady of the windy day
Sets my heart on fire
She pauses in her every breath
And I listen to her silence

death.line: I watched you hold the sun in your arms while he bled to death
stanza: I watched you hold the sun in your arms while he bled to death
He grew so pale next to you
The world is so pale next to you
Well, what is this craziness?
This crazy talking?
You caught some small death
When you were sleepwalking
